subject: Clarify hosted rate-card: Chat Completions vs Responses vs legacy endpoints
messages:
From: Joel Simmons <joel.simmons@boxedgoods.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API price breakdown request — need chat vs responses clarity

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the quick demo yesterday. Procurement asked me for a clear line-item breakdown of how Redwood bills the different generation endpoints. Specifically they want: 1) how Chat Completions map to tokens and cost, 2) how the new 'Responses' endpoint is metered versus the legacy 'Completions' endpoints, and 3) whether embedding or KV caching changes unit accounting for hosted customers.

Can you send a single-page summary or the rate card that shows conversion examples (prompt tokens, response tokens, per-token rate, and any per-request or per-call charges)? We're preparing a 12-month committed usage decision and need to model costs for 3 forecasted workloads (support triage, search rerank, and product copy generation).

If it's easier, we can do a 30-minute call this afternoon — procurement is in PST.

Thanks,
Joel
Procurement Lead — BoxedGoods Inc
[Attachment: RFQ_BoxedGoods_0427.pdf (PDF, 34 KB)]

From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Joel Simmons <joel.simmons@boxedgoods.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API price breakdown request — need chat vs responses clarity

Joel —

Appreciate the note and the RFQ. I've attached our most recent rate card (Redwood_Ratecard_v2.pdf) which includes a conversion table and worked examples. Short answers to your bullets so procurement can start modeling today: 

- Chat Completions: metered per-token (prompt + completion). The billed units count both input context tokens and generated tokens; costs are shown as $/1k tokens on the rate card.
- Responses endpoint: designed for simpler integration patterns — billed per-response token with a slightly different discount band and optional per-call processing fee for features like function/tool-calling. The rate card includes a per-1k-token equivalent so you can compare one-to-one with chat.
- Legacy Completions: older endpoints map similarly to tokens but may have different pricing tiers and are being consolidated; see the legacy mapping table on page 4 of the rate card.
- Embeddings and KV/prefix caching: embeddings are billed separately as embedding units (see embedders table). KV/prefix caching reduces total billed prompt tokens observed by the runtime (so your effective cost drops) but does not introduce a separate hidden unit — savings appear as fewer prompt tokens on usage reports.

I'll highlight two worked examples in the rate card that match the workloads you mentioned, but if you want a pro-forma model for each workload with your expected monthly volumes, Marissa can put numbers into our cost-estimator spreadsheet. Would you like us to pre-fill that with your RFQ numbers?

If procurement prefers a call, I'm available at 2:00pm PST for a 25–30 minute run-through.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_Ratecard_v2.pdf (PDF, 78 KB)]

From: Joel Simmons <joel.simmons@boxedgoods.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@boxedgoods.com
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API price breakdown request — need chat vs responses clarity

Olga / team —

Thanks — the rate card is helpful. A few quick clarifications from procurement: 

1) For the Responses endpoint, is the "per-call processing fee" always applied when function/tool-calling is enabled, or is that waived under committed contracts?
2) For committed-usage pricing, do chat and responses both share the same committed pool (i.e., can credits be used interchangeably), or are they siloed to endpoint families?
3) We're evaluating a 24-month commitment for ~$120k/mo baseline consumption. What discount bands can we expect (ballpark) and what SLAs/overage handling come with that level of commit?

We want a defensible number to present to finance by next Tuesday. If needed, Ben and Marissa are welcome to join the call.

—Joel

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Joel Simmons <joel.simmons@boxedgoods.com>
Cc: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 17 Apr 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API price breakdown request — need chat vs responses clarity

Joel — thanks for the follow-ups. I'll keep this high-level here and attach the contract-ready language in the SOW draft.

1) Processing fee on Responses + function-calls: For enterprise committed agreements we can waive the per-call processing fee for standard function-calling patterns (JSON returns, tool calls under 5 per response) — we'll treat heavier tool usage as an add-on that we model separately. We'll call that out explicitly in the SOW.

2) Committed pool: We can offer a single committed token pool that covers both Chat Completions and Responses for hosted customers — converted to a unified 1k-token equivalent on invoices. That means your commit dollars apply across endpoints (we do per-endpoint reporting, but not siloed billing).

3) Discount bands & SLAs: At your stated baseline ($120k/mo, 24-month) here's an indicative structure (finals subject to legal/finance):
   - 10–12% off list for a 12–18 month commit at the $120k/mo baseline
   - 15–20% off list for 24+ months with minimum annualization and predictable consumption profile
   - Enterprise SLA (99.9% uptime for hosted API, regional failover options) and a dedicated success engineer for onboarding and performance tuning

I've attached a draft SOW and an example usage-to-cost worksheet that maps three workload patterns to monthly spend under both chat and responses assumptions. Marissa will follow up with an itemized cost model and can pre-populate it with the RFQ numbers you attached.

If that sounds reasonable, can we schedule a short alignment call Monday morning so finance has the deck Monday afternoon?

Best regards,
Ben Carter
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SOW_BoxedGoods_Draft.docx (DOCX, 42 KB)]
